issue.title: Duplicate dict key trips ruff F601 in the ownership audit test, blocking every commit repo-wide
issue.description:
REPRODUCTION (clean origin/master a0b6cd16b, no local changes):

    .venv/bin/ruff check tests/test_agent_artifact_directory_operation_audit.py
    F601 Dictionary key literal repeated
       --> tests/test_agent_artifact_directory_operation_audit.py:292:5

ROOT CAUSE: _REVIEWED_DIR_OPERATION_CONTEXTS contains the key
'src/sase/workspace_provider/reset_replay.py:_clear_owned_paths' TWICE, at lines 279 and
292, with different exemption prose. The second entry was added by b82f21c1b 'test:
register ownership audit coverage' (from the now-closed epic sase-mq) on top of an entry
that already existed. The second entry is also out of keep-sorted order, sitting after
the utils.py key.

IMPACT: this project sets commit_hooks.before: 'just fix' in sase/sase.yml. 'just fix'
runs 'ruff check --fix src/ tests/', F601 has no autofix, so the recipe exits 1 and the
before-commit hook fails. Every 'sase stitch create' / sase_git_commit in this repo
fails for every agent until this is fixed, regardless of what the agent changed. There
is no sanctioned bypass: sase stitch create has no hook-skip flag, the commit workflow
reads no skip env var, and project-local config has the highest merge precedence so a
user-global override cannot neutralize it. Discovered when a documentation-only refresh
could not be committed.

FIX: delete one of the two entries. Note that Python already discards the FIRST one, so
deleting line 279's entry preserves current runtime behavior exactly and is
semantically a no-op; deleting line 292's entry instead CHANGES which exemption the
audit enforces. The two exemptions say materially different things (line 279: 'Clears
only caller-supplied paths after resolving and verifying each path is inside the live
leased checkout...'; line 292: 'Clears only caller-supplied generated paths after
reset-and-replay has authorized a live leased checkout...'), so a human should confirm
which text is authoritative rather than deleting arbitrarily. Restore keep-sorted order
for the surviving entry.

VERIFY: 'just fix' exits 0, and
tests/test_agent_artifact_directory_operation_audit.py::test_artifact_directory_operation_sites_are_reviewed
still passes.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-n1 — same file and same dict key. sase-n1 reports the entry MISSING (audit test failed); this bead reports it present TWICE (ruff F601). Whoever fixes either should read both, since the surviving entry must satisfy sase-n1's review requirement.
RELATED: sase-mq — closed epic whose landed commit b82f21c1b 'test: register ownership audit coverage' introduced the second duplicate entry.

PROVENANCE CORRECTION + A SECOND FILE BROKEN BY THE SAME COMMIT, AND A VERIFIED FIX IS READY (from sase-m6.7.1.3, 2026-08-16).

1. The duplicate entry did NOT come from b82f21c1b. 'git show b82f21c1b -- tests/test_agent_artifact_directory_operation_audit.py' is +8/-0 and added the FIRST entry (the one that survives, prose 'Clears only caller-supplied generated paths after reset-and-replay has authorized a live leased checkout...'). 'git show a0b6cd16b -- tests/test_agent_artifact_directory_operation_audit.py' is +7/-0 and added the SECOND, out-of-order entry at line 292 (prose 'Clears only caller-supplied paths after resolving and verifying each path is inside the live leased checkout; reset-and-replay already refuses primary, unclaimed, and non-operational contexts'). b82f21c1b landed 05:11, a0b6cd16b landed 06:55. This matters for the fix: delete the line-292 entry and keep the line-285 one, which is the reviewed text from the ownership epic.

2. Why a0b6cd16b added it: that commit is mine (relation-panel phase sase-m6.7.1.3), authored in a workspace whose checkout predated b82f21c1b, so the agent hit the genuine audit failure sase-n1 describes and independently added its own entry. The same staleness clobbered a SECOND file in the same commit, which sase-n2 does not yet cover:

   tests/workspace_provider/test_workspace_lease.py — a0b6cd16b reverted 18 lines back to the pre-71012c5c7 text. 71012c5c7 'refactor(workspace): narrow operational lease internals' (epic sase-mq.8, the immediate parent commit) privatized the lease helpers and rewrote the test bodies to use the aliased public names. a0b6cd16b put the private names (_OperationalLeaseError, _authorize_operational_lease_workspace, _bind_operational_lease, _transfer_operational_lease) back into the test BODIES while leaving 71012c5c7's import block, which aliases those private names to public ones. Result on current master: 10 tests in that file fail with NameError.

3. A verified fix for both files exists in workspace sase_14 right now. Each file is restored byte-for-byte to its 71012c5c7 content ('git diff 71012c5c7 -- <both files>' is empty). Verified on that tree: repo-wide '.venv/bin/ruff check src/ tests/' clean; both files pass (20 passed); and a full 'just check-full' passed every lint gate (fmt, keep-sorted, ruff, mypy, symvision, toobig, sase validation) with 30960 passed / 11 skipped / 3 failed, the 3 being the tracked process-global config-cache flake sase-mv and nothing else. Awaiting the project owner's go-ahead to commit.

VERIFIED ON CURRENT MASTER (30c9ba23b, working tree clean, while closing sase-n1): the F601 duplicate is already gone. 467f8c184 deleted the second, out-of-order _clear_owned_paths entry that a0b6cd16b added, leaving the single b82f21c1b exemption. '.venv/bin/ruff check tests/test_agent_artifact_directory_operation_audit.py' is clean and test_artifact_directory_operation_sites_are_reviewed passes. Whoever works this bead can confirm and close without a further code change.
